https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/lithuan.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.09.02 17:12 Lithuania's skies in the crosshairs: innovators to respond to airspace threats Source: Delfi EN Flaming Shield Defence Innovation Hackathon PHOTO: Vidmantas Činauskas Pranešimas spaudai Follow Delfi on Google Unidentified drones, smuggling balloons, scrambled NATO fighter jets and temporarily halted airport operations – airspace incidents in the Baltic region are no longer isolated events, but a challenge demanding ever-faster solutions. On October 9–11 in Kaunas, more than 300 technology developers, defence experts and innovators will search for a technological answer: how to detect, identify and assess potential threats in Lithuania's airspace as early as possible. Airspace security will be the focus of this year’s Flaming Shield, the defence innovation hackathon organised for the fourth time by the Lithuanian Riflemen’s Union (LŠS) and Tech-Park Kaunas. This year’s strategic mission: Defend the Sky. Defend the Sky – the 2026 Mission Hackathon participants will develop solutions across eight thematic tracks related to the detection, identification and classification of aerial objects, the integration of artificial intelligence, data management, and resilient communication systems. Attention will also be given to civil protection and dual-use solutions for critical infrastructure. According to Colonel Linas Idzelis, Commander of the Lithuanian Riflemen’s Union, the role of technology in modern conflicts is fundamentally changing how defence must be prepared for. "We see very clear trends in countries at war – advanced technology has long since become a primary weapon. That is why this year’s hackathon sets participants a central goal: a secure sky. We are bringing together the brightest minds, innovators and defence experts to take strong first steps in developing new unmanned systems, their detection systems and robotics – covering the full spectrum, from sea and land to space," says Col. Linas Idzelis, Commander of the Lithuanian Riflemen’s Union. The experience of the three previous hackathons shows that Flaming Shield has become not only a venue for intensive technology development, but also a meeting point for different participants in the defence innovation ecosystem. Teams are supported by dozens of mentors and specialists, can present their ideas to potential investors and partners, and the most promising solutions have the opportunity to continue development after the hackathon ends. Tech-Park Kaunas director Paulius Nezabitauskas stresses that today it is especially important to shorten the path from a technological idea to its testing under real conditions – and to bring together, in one place, developers, the defence sector, investors and the public sector. "Air defence is no longer an abstract subject from news about other countries – it has become an everyday reality that every region of Lithuania has faced this year. Business and science have the technological potential to respond quickly to such challenges, but they often lack the space where an idea can become a working prototype within days, and then a proven solution. The hackathon’s value lies not only in the prototypes it produces, but in the connections it builds between developers, the military, investors and the public sector – connections formed here in three days rather than months," says P. Nezabitauskas. Three Days – From Problem to Prototype Flaming Shield will open on October 9 with the Tech Demo Day event, where representatives of the defence, technology and public sectors, together with international experts, will discuss the most pressing airspace security challenges, opportunities for startups and small companies in the European defence market, and investment in defence innovation. On October 10–11, teams will move into an intensive 48-hour working period – from a chosen challenge and initial idea through to a prototype and its final presentation to a panel of experts. Running in parallel is Cyber Arena – a cybersecurity competition organised by the LŠS cybersecurity unit "Lizdeika" together with the National Cyber Security Centre (NKSC). Professionals and advanced enthusiasts will compete across three disciplines: Capture the Flag, Bug Bounty and King of the Hill. In the classic CTF track, participants will tackle cryptography, web vulnerability, reverse engineering and other tasks. In the Bug Bounty track, they will search for vulnerabilities in real, live organisational systems, while in King of the Hill, teams will need to seize control of systems in real time – and hold on to it for as long as possible. Not Just Prizes – A Path to Grow the Idea Further Participants will develop solutions across eight thematic tracks – from the detection and classification of aerial objects and the development of drones and robotics, to data fusion and command-and-control (C2) systems, resilient communications, threat neutralisation, and cyber- and space-layer as well as civil protection solutions. Challenges were submitted, and prizes established, by companies of strategic importance to Lithuania – among them the Ignalina Nuclear Power Plant (ALTRA), the Lithuanian Defence and Security Industry Association, the Lithuanian Naval Force, and others. The hackathon’s total prize fund exceeds €15,000, and among the event’s sponsors and partners are well-known Lithuanian technology companies Omnisend, Oxylabs, Surfshark and others. Vinted, meanwhile, will award prizes to the best-performing participants and teams in the Cyber Arena track. But cash prizes are only one of the opportunities on offer. In 2025, the strongest hackathon teams were able to compete for an invitation from venture capital fund Coinvest Capital to negotiate investments of up to €750,000 – and the investment firm will again be seeking promising teams at this year’s event. "Coinvest Capital was the first in the region to start investing in defence technologies, so today we see with particular clarity how important every timely local innovation is. Our key priority is to support and invest in the local defence innovation industry and the development of its capabilities: only by nurturing and strengthening technologies developed in Lithuania can we ensure the country’s genuine resilience. That is why, once again, at the Flaming Shield hackathon we will be looking for the strongest teams ready to turn these ideas into working solutions," says Coinvest Capital CEO Viktorija Trimbel. The hackathon also opens a path for participants into the wider European and NATO defence innovation ecosystem – NATO DIANA (the Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic), the EU Defence Innovation Scheme (EUDIS), and the Nordic-Baltic initiative ODIN. From Hackathon to Million-Euro Investment Flaming Shield has been held since 2023 and will take place this year for the fourth time. Previous editions have shown that an idea born during a few intensive days of work can go on to have a life beyond the event itself. At the 2024 hackathon, solutions developed included FPV-drone-based technologies, among others, with a main prize fund of €45,000 awarded to the best teams. The 2025 edition grew into a broader cycle of defence innovation events, bringing together developers, startups, investors, and senior Lithuanian and international defence experts. Hackathon alumni – Luna Robotics, Astrolight, Broswarm, PDKinematics, TD Autonomy and others – have already raised more than €7 million in investment. The organisers’ goal is that this year, too, the prototypes built over 48 hours should not end with the presentation to the expert panel. The most promising teams will be able to pursue further investment, partners, technology-testing opportunities and additional paths to develop their solutions further. Registration for the hackathon is open until October 1. The event will take place October 9–11 in Kaunas. Strategic partners – Omnisend and the Lithuanian Defence and Security Industry Association. Cyber Arena main sponsor – Vinted. Photograph: Suzanne Plunkett/Reuters Barclays Barclays softens return-to-office plans for UK staff after backlash Bank allows employees to delay being in workplace at least three days a week until 2027, if permission granted Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent Tue 29 Sep 2026 13.12 EDT Last modified on Tue 29 Sep 2026 13.14 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Barclays has watered down its return-to-office plans after a major staff backlash , with the bank allowing some employees to wait until next year before having to be in at least three days a week. The bank this summer announced the attendance requirement would come in for its 45,000 UK staff from 5 October, with more senior employees expected to come in for at least four days. That compares with current rules requiring staff to come in for two. Now Barclays has offered a reprieve after thousands of bank staff signed an open letter drafted by the Unite union, calling for payouts to help cover travel costs and an exemption for those living more than 40 minutes from work. The bank will allow staff to delay complying with the order until 2027. However, they will need to ask and receive permission to do so from their line manager by the end of this week. In a memo emailed to staff, Barclays’ executive committee announced: “We are extending the implementation period for UK colleagues to ensure colleagues have the right support as we move through the transition … We are also reviewing our flexible working policy.” The extension, first reported by the Financial Times, could give unions more time to request further concessions. Barclays and Unite said they would continue discussions on the issue, which has become a flashpoint across the banking sector. Banks ranging from JP Morgan to Revolut have clamped down on remote working after the Covid pandemic, arguing it harmed the training of younger staff. Unite have said that while they recognise face-to-face working can support collaboration, team development and relationship building: “We do not accept that this requires a blanket, one-size-fits-all increase in mandatory office attendance.” The union has requested a series of concessions, including: automatic exemptions of in-office attendance rules during school holidays and Christmas; capping in-office requirements at one day a week for any carers or people with disabilities; flexible start and finish times to allow for cheaper off-peak travel costs and to accommodate school pickup and drop-offs; subsidised onsite meal costs; and a single, consolidated payment made to all staff to make up for the costs of coming into the office, before March 2027. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion A spokesperson said: “Unite is continuing to engage with Barclays on its proposals relating to colleagues’ working arrangements.” In an emailed statement, a Barclays spokesperson said: “Our updated onsite working arrangements will take effect as planned. “We have continued to listen to colleague feedback to ensure colleagues have the right support while enabling us to deliver the benefits of working together in person. After posting 211-6 backed by Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 20 balls and a late effort from Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube, India restricted Pakistan to 192-6 despite a big knock of 96 off 51 balls from Hasan Nawaz. India's Abhishek Sharma propelled his side into a comfortable pace by hitting 61 off just 20 balls Image: Anushree Fadnavis/REUTERS Nawaz fell four runs short of a century on the final ball of the innings, when he was caught by wicketkeeper Sanju Samson off Dube's bowling. It marked Pakistan's first-ever appearance in a men's Asian Games cricket final. The event also marked one of the game's fiercest rivalries played out on an unlikely stage: a converted baseball field in suburban Nagoya, where Indians and Pakistanis living in Japan queued for hours to fill the 2,500-capacity venue. "I think this is never going to happen again, India against Pakistan in Japan," Pakistan supporter Umer Dar, a 26-year-old Nagoya resident, told AFP. "Even if it's in Japan, the craze of India versus Pakistan is always there," added Tokyo-based India fan Afroz Khan. "Anywhere they play in the world, it's always crazy." While cricket remains a niche sport in Japan, there has been growing local interest, as shown by India's first-ever T20 international against Japan last week, which India won by just two runs in a rain-shortened match. https://p.dw.com/p/5NgtF Skip next section Pranavi Urs scripts history, wins Asian Games golf gold 10/03/2026 October 3, 2026 Pranavi Urs scripts history, wins Asian Games golf gold Seerat Chabba India's Pranavi Urs took gold in the women's individual final Image: Andy Chua/REUTERS Pranavi Urs has become the first Indian woman to win gold in the Asian Games individual golf after she sank a nerve-wracking three-foot par putt on the final green to clinch the title by one stroke, finishing at 15-under par. Teammates Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar celebrated by soaking Urs with water as her win was confirmed. China's Yin Ruoning and Singapore's Shannon Tan tied for silver and bronze a stroke back, with Yin claiming silver after a playoff. This is India's first gold in the sport since Shiv Kapur's men's title in 2002. Urs, Ashok and Dagar also came together to win India its first-ever team silver in the event. China won team gold, with Taiwan's team, featuring five-time major champion Tseng Ya-ni, taking bronze. https://p.dw.com/p/5Ngqe Skip next section CJP calls for mass Delhi march on October 10 10/03/2026 October 3, 2026 CJP calls for mass Delhi march on October 10 Seerat Chabba The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced it will mobilize a nationwide march on New Delhi next weekend unless Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. The call follows a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park that drew thousands of demonstrators despite police denying permission for the gathering. A similar protest at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar saw several opposition politicians and student leaders being detained on Friday, which is also observed as Gandhi Jayanti to honor the birth of Mahatma Gandhi, a global pioneer of nonviolence. Local police detained several demonstrators in New Delhi Image: Bhawika Chhabra/REUTERS "If Gyanesh Kumar doesn't resign, cockroaches from across India will march to Delhi and protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10," CJP founder and convener Abhijeet Dipke said in the statement. "And if the Delhi Police tries to stop us, wherever they stop us will become our Jantar Mantar. Ours will be a peaceful protest. We will walk on the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi." Calling on people to join the march to preserve free and fair elections in the country, Dipke called it "a fight to save our democracy." The announcement follows a tense October 2, when Delhi Police detained more than 700 demonstrators, including former Delhi Chief Minister Atishi, from Jantar Mantar and surrounding areas, local media reported. Police had denied permission for the Delhi gathering and imposed Section 163 restrictions barring assemblies of more than five people. The CJP-led gathering in Mumbai's Shivaji Park also saw a huge turnout, including film actors and musicians, but did not face a similar violent crackdown from authorities. It is the latest flashpoint in a months-long movement that began as online satire in May and escalated into repeated street demonstrations, including a July 20 protest where Delhi Police used batons to disperse crowds. It led to the resignation of India's then-Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in late July. https://p.dw.com/p/5NgnT Skip next section Welcome to our coverage 10/03/2026 October 3, 2026 Welcome to our coverage Seerat Chabba Hello! https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.text: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Kazakhstan, Czech Republic sign deal to expand railway cooperation Kazakhstan News 16 October 2026 10:08 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Ministry of Transport of Kazakhstan Alyona Pavlenko Journalist, International Desk Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 16 . Kazakhstan and the Czech Republic have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at developing cooperation in railway transport, industry, and technological development, the Kazakh Ministry of Transport reported. The document was signed following a bilateral meeting between Kazakh Minister of Transport Nurlan Sauranbaev and Czech Minister of Transport Ivan Bednárik on the sidelines of the international transport and logistics business forum New Silk Way in Astana. During the meeting, the ministers discussed prospects for expanding bilateral cooperation in the transport sector, including civil aviation and railway transport. The memorandum is intended to provide a basis for further strengthening bilateral ties and expanding mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries in the transport sector. Separately, the Delegation of the European Union to Kazakhstan reported that EU Ambassador to Kazakhstan Aleška Simkić met with Bednárik in Astana during his visit to the country. According to the delegation, the Czech minister's visit was part of a regional economic diplomacy mission aimed at strengthening transport cooperation, exploring new business opportunities, and promoting Czech expertise and technologies in transport and logistics. During his meeting with Simkić, the participants exchanged views on transport connectivity between Europe and Central Asia, including the development of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor and opportunities for cooperation under the European Union's Global Gateway strategy. Bednárik also spoke at the New Silk Way Business Forum.
